research_scope: Five complete contextual source-free reviews: representability, pushouts, iso-comma categories, 2-fibre products and 2-finality. No new definitions, external research, or automatic aliases.

references.context: Category theory: ordinary category with objects, morphisms, identities and associative composition, without requiring its collection of objects to be a set; any size assumptions are stated separately.
references.matching_note: Source occurrence 'category C' denotes an ordinary category without a smallness requirement. Existing small-category meaning is too restrictive; do not conflate a fibred category, groupoid or slice category with the ambient category.
references.reason: The available small-category meaning would impose extra hypotheses not supplied by this definition.

references.context: Category theory: covariant functor from an arbitrary category C to Sets, assigning sets to objects and functions to arrows, preserving identities and composition; do not impose source-category smallness.
references.reason: The indexed covariant functor is restricted to small source categories, whereas this formula does not impose smallness.
references.matching_note: Source-free provisional prerequisite. Compare globally with the reviewed missing unrestricted-functor candidate; do not automatically alias.

references.context: Category theory: natural isomorphism between two covariant set-valued functors, a natural transformation with an inverse natural transformation; in particular its component bijections satisfy naturality in Y.
references.reason: Pointwise bijections without naturality are insufficient for representability.
references.matching_note: Source-free typed dependency; audit naturality and domain-size conventions later.

references.context: Category theory: collection Hom_C(X,Y) of morphisms from X to Y in C, which must be set-valued for this representable functor; a possibly large category need not globally be small.
references.reason: Representability uses a Hom-functor, and the indexed small-category hom-set candidate must not be treated as a general size-unrestricted category.
references.matching_note: Compare with the separately recorded small-category hom-set and compact-object Hom occurrences in global alias audit.

references.disposition: Existential quantification over objects of C is ordinary categorical mathematical language, not a new contextual meaning.

references.phrase: morphisms B to A and B to C
references.context: Category theory: a span or common-domain arrow diagram B→A and B→C in an arbitrary category, not a composable arrow pair and not the dual cospan.
references.reason: The shape of the input diagram is a reusable categorical construction distinct from the pushout being defined.

references.phrase: morphisms A to P and C to P agreeing on B
references.context: Category theory: cocone over the span B→A,B→C, namely arrows A→P,C→P whose composites from B agree.
references.reason: A compatible cocone is input data in a categorical pushout universal property.
references.matching_note: Keep the cocone separate from its colimiting universal property and from the opposite limit cone.

references.phrase: every other compatible pair factors uniquely
references.disposition: This is the universal uniqueness clause *defining this pushout*. It asserts unique mediating maps for each other cocone, not a separately presupposed object or an independent 'unique-factorization domain' concept. Recheck source-local dispositions in the global audit.
P is the defined output object; it is not itself an additional missing contextual meaning.

references.reason: The categorical isomorphism α is an independent prerequisite, distinct from a bare bijection between underlying sets.

references.reason: The compatibility condition is a commutative-square construction used for the morphisms of the iso-comma category.
references.matching_note: Candidate is a typed commutativity/coherence condition, not an arbitrary unstructured pair of arrows.

references.context: Higher category theory: invertible comparison 2-cell between the composites W→X→Z and W→Y→Z in a (2,1)-category; every 2-cell there is invertible, but the specified comparison is still part of the pseudocone data.
references.reason: The source requires a specific 2-isomorphism, not merely equality of composite 1-arrows.
references.matching_note: Audit against the existing candidate for invertible 2-morphisms in a strict 2-category; do not conflate source restrictions.

references.context: Higher category theory: pseudocone over a cospan X→Z←Y from an object W, consisting of 1-cells W→X,W→Y and an invertible comparison 2-cell of their composites to Z.
references.reason: The two legs together with their 2-cell are prerequisite structured test data for the universal 2-fibre product.
references.matching_note: Do not identify this with an ordinary strictly commuting 1-category cone.

references.disposition: Existence of a 1-cell from every Y to T is precisely a quantifier clause of the definition of 2-finality, while the ambient (2,1)-category is already linked. It is not a separately named prerequisite.

This is the defining uniqueness clause for 2-finality (equivalent to contractibility of the hom-groupoid in this setting). Do not confuse it with ordinary 1-categorical terminality or suppress reusable invertible-2-cell dependencies elsewhere.
The special (2,1)-categorical final-object property is the meaning being defined; ordinary 1-category finality is not its dependency.
